findings.description: The upper tail of F is the only tail F has, so no one-tailed reading rescues this. findings.notes: THE MODELLING ASSUMPTION IS DOING THE WORK AND MUST BE STATED: this reads df2 as n_observations - 2, the residual df of a simple linear regression of n-back level on session number, which is what 'the specific training gain was well explained by a linear function' most naturally describes. findings.description: absence_of_evidence is the right check and could not be run on any of the four: it requires a confidence interval, or a coefficient with its standard error, and the paper prints only bounds on F with no effect size, no interval, and in one case no df. findings.title: Outcome data only in figures (Figures 2 and 3)
findings.description: The paper contains no tables at all; the PDF extraction returned zero. This is the single largest coverage limit on this review. With the group means, SDs and ns, GRIM and GRIMMER would apply directly (the Gf score is a count of correct solutions, an integer), recalc_independent_t and rivets_independent_t could test the reported t values against the group statistics, and check_effect_plausibility could test the printed Cohen's d for internal consistency. None of that was possible. Values read off the bars would carry figure_pixels provenance and are barred from the exact-arithmetic family, so digitising them would not recover these checks.

findings.title: No preregistration or data availability (Front matter and Acknowledgments)
findings.description: The paper states two hypotheses in advance (transfer, and dose-dependence) and both are treated as confirmatory in this review's anatomy on the strength of the abstract, but no registration or protocol is cited, so the distinction between confirmatory and exploratory rests on the paper's own framing. This is unremarkable for a 2008 publication -- preregistration was not a norm in this field at the time -- and is recorded for completeness rather than as a criticism. No data-availability statement is present and no supplementary files accompany the article.
